story: North Slope Power, the North Slope Borough's planned 3 GW gas plant for AI data centers, its public money and its partner's campaign contributions, days before borough residents vote on the mayor

claims.claim: Twenty First Century Utilities is the North Slope Borough's corporate partner in North Slope Power, which is developing a 3 gigawatt (3,000 megawatt) natural gas plant.
claims.verbatim: Twenty First Century Utilities (TFC), the borough's corporate partner in North Slope Power, which is developing a 3 gigawatt natural gas plant with plans to scale to a world record-breaking 10 gigawatts
claims.notes: Byline on the page is Lauren Windsor. In window. The 3 GW figure is corroborated independently by Dermot Cole on May 12th (C21). No primary North Slope Power or TFC document was reachable; twentyfirstcenturyutilities.com does not resolve in DNS and the borough resolutions sit on a SharePoint viewer that returns no text. Checked 2026-10-04. The megawatt figure is the unit conversion of the reported 3 gigawatts.

claims.claim: North Slope Power plans to scale the plant to 10 gigawatts (10,000 megawatts).
claims.verbatim: with plans to scale to a world record-breaking 10 gigawatts
claims.suggested_phrasing: plans to scale to 10 gigawatts, which the Alaska Current calls world record-breaking
claims.notes: 10 GW corroborated by Dermot Cole (C21). 'world record-breaking' belongs to the outlet and no published capacity figure for the world's largest gas plant was verified, so the superlative is attributed or dropped. Derived and not a source fact, 10,000 MW is about 3.5 times Alaska's 2024 net summer capacity of 2,853 MW (C25), and 3,000 MW alone slightly exceeds it. NSP figures are presumably nameplate and EIA's is net summer capacity, so the comparison is approximate. The megawatt figure is the unit conversion of the reported 10 gigawatts.

claims.claim: Twenty First Century Utilities specializes in building energy infrastructure for data centers.
claims.verbatim: TFC specializes in building energy infrastructure for data centers.
claims.suggested_phrasing: TFC, which the Alaska Current describes as specializing in energy infrastructure for data centers
claims.notes: Outlet characterisation of the company; TFC's own site could not be reached (DNS failure).

claims.claim: The project would tap nearly 30 trillion cubic feet of proven natural gas reserves in Prudhoe Bay, according to the Alaska Current.
claims.verbatim: The project will tap into nearly 30 trillion cubic feet of proven natural gas reserves in Prudhoe Bay
claims.suggested_phrasing: nearly 30 trillion cubic feet of proven reserves in Prudhoe Bay, according to the Alaska Current
claims.notes: Not reconciled with C22. Dermot Cole gives more than 35 trillion cubic feet for the North Slope as a whole, a different geography. Attribute each figure to its outlet.

claims.claim: North Slope Power would deliver electricity to colocated AI data centers.
claims.verbatim: to deliver electricity to colocated AI data centers, which are notoriously energy and water intensive
claims.notes: Corroborated by Dermot Cole (C20). 'notoriously energy and water intensive' is the outlet's characterisation and is not carried as fact.

claims.claim: One planning document lists integrated regional microgrids and a second natural gas pipeline to Utqiagvik as other elements of the project.
claims.value: a second natural gas pipeline to Utqiagvik
claims.verbatim: According to one of the documents, other elements of the project include the construction of integrated regional microgrids and a second natural gas pipeline to Utqiaġvik, formerly known as Barrow
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to planning documents obtained by the Alaska Current
claims.notes: Single outlet, citing a document it obtained that is not published.

claims.claim: Mayor Josiah Patkotak authorized a no-bid contract for TFC to conduct a feasibility study in November 2025.
claims.verbatim: In Nov. 2025, Patkotak authorized a $1.2 million no-bid contract for the firm to conduct a feasibility study.
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to the Alaska Current
claims.notes: Event dated November 2025, background to the window. The Current links borough document 84-2025.pdf on sp.north-slope.org; that SharePoint viewer returned no text, so the primary was not reached.

claims.claim: In March the North Slope Borough committed another $5 million in public funds to TFC to move forward in developing North Slope Power.
claims.verbatim: In March, the North Slope Borough committed another $5 million in public funds to Twenty First Century Utilities to move forward in developing North Slope Power.
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to the Alaska Current
claims.notes: The linked resolution file is 13-2026.pdf on sp.north-slope.org; the viewer returned only the filename, so the primary was not reached. Running total from C07 and C08 is $6.2 million (derived).

claims.claim: The resolution authorizing the $5 million contract described North Slope Power as an investor-owned utility with Borough majority ownership.
claims.verbatim: The resolution authorizing the contract described the utility as "an investor-owned utility (IOU) with Borough majority ownership."
claims.suggested_phrasing: the resolution, as quoted by the Alaska Current, describes
claims.notes: Resolution language quoted second-hand. Primary (NSB Resolution 13-2026) not readable.

claims.claim: The resolution said North Slope Power would be structured so that the Borough would initially maintain a majority ownership interest.
claims.value: initially maintain a majority ownership interest
claims.verbatim: North Slope Power would be "structured so that the Borough would initially maintain a majority ownership interest," indicating a future transition to majority ownership by outside investors.
claims.suggested_phrasing: the word 'initially', which the Alaska Current reads as pointing to later outside majority ownership
claims.notes: The quoted clause is the resolution's text as reproduced by the Current. The inference about a future transition is the outlet's reading, not a stated plan, and must be attributed if used.

claims.claim: The financial structure of the deal between the North Slope Borough and TFC is not public.
claims.verbatim: The financial structure of the deal between North Slope Borough and Twenty First Century Utilities is not public, but there are clues emerging.
claims.suggested_phrasing: the financial structure has not been made public, according to the Alaska Current
claims.notes: The Alaska Current reported on May 12th that the borough would tap its Permanent Fund (C24). Treat both as reporting, not as a disclosed term sheet.

claims.claim: TFC managing partner Peter Corsell, his wife Betsy Cragon and his business partner Larry Kellerman each donated $5,000 to Mayor Patkotak on December 31st, 2025.
claims.verbatim: According to the Alaska Public Offices Commission campaign disclosure portal, TFC Managing Partner Peter Corsell, his wife Betsy Cragon, and his business partner Larry Kellerman each donated $5,000 to Mayor Patkotak on Dec. 31, 2025.
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to APOC filings reported by the Alaska Current
claims.notes: The APOC portal shows only a search form to a fetcher, so the filings could not be confirmed directly. Single outlet citing a public record.

claims.claim: TFC partner Ross Berger contributed $500 to Mayor Patkotak on December 21st, 2025.
claims.verbatim: Another TFC partner, Ross Berger, contributed $500 on Dec. 21, 2025
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to APOC filings reported by the Alaska Current
claims.notes: Same sourcing limit as C12.

claims.claim: Contributions from TFC people totalled $15,500, about 27 percent of the $57,610 Patkotak reported raising.
claims.verbatim: bringing Patkotak's haul from TFC to $15,500, which is about 27% of his total reported raise of $57,610
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to APOC filings reported by the Alaska Current
claims.notes: Arithmetic checks, 3 x $5,000 + $500 = $15,500, and 15,500 / 57,610 = 26.9 percent. The $57,610 total is the outlet's figure from APOC and was not confirmed on the portal.

claims.claim: TFC's proposal listed climate change among 10 North Slope challenges and later wrote N/A next to it where it outlined how it was tackling each one.
claims.verbatim: Later in the deck, TFC again listed those 10 challenges, but this time outlined how it is tackling each of them. Next to climate change, Twenty First Century Utilities wrote "N/A."
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to the proposal as described by the Alaska Current
claims.notes: The Current places the challenge list on slides 22 and 23 of TFC's proposal, a document it obtained and did not publish. Single outlet.

claims.claim: North Slope Borough residents vote on Tuesday on whether to oust Mayor Josiah Patkotak, according to the Alaska Current.
claims.verbatim: On Tuesday, residents of the North Slope Borough (NSB) will decide whether to oust their mayor, Josiah Patkotak.
claims.suggested_phrasing: North Slope Borough voters go to the polls Tuesday, with the mayor's seat at stake, according to the Alaska Current
claims.notes: October 3rd, 2026 was a Saturday, so Tuesday is October 6th (derived). Whether this is the regular mayoral election or a recall, and who the other candidates are, could not be verified on any primary record. Do not name the election type or opponents.

claims.claim: Patkotak weathered two recall efforts in early 2025.
claims.verbatim: the incumbent weathered two recall efforts in early 2025
claims.suggested_phrasing: survived two recall efforts in early 2025, the Alaska Current reports
claims.notes: Background, not independently confirmed.

claims.claim: Corsell, Kellerman and Patkotak did not respond to the Alaska Current's requests for comment.
claims.verbatim: Corsell, Kellerman, and Patkotak did not respond to requests for comment.
claims.notes: Fairness context for any slide on the contributions.

claims.claim: Dermot Cole reported that the North Slope Borough maps a plan for what he called the largest natural gas power plant in the world.
claims.value: largest natural gas power plant in the world
claims.verbatim: North Slope maps plan for largest natural gas power plant in the world
claims.suggested_phrasing: billed as what would be the world's largest gas-fired power plant
claims.notes: Background, outside the window. Headline superlative; no comparison figure verified.

claims.claim: Cole reported the plant would sit near Prudhoe Bay and generate electricity for industry, data centers and potentially a power line to the Railbelt.
claims.value: a power line to the Railbelt
claims.verbatim: near Prudhoe Bay, which would generate electricity for industry, data centers and potentially a power line to the Railbelt
claims.suggested_phrasing: potentially a power line south to the Railbelt
claims.notes: Background. The Railbelt line is a possibility in Cole's account, not a plan.

claims.claim: Cole reported a 3 gigawatt first phase that could be expanded to 10 gigawatts.
claims.verbatim: 3 gigawatt first phase that could be expanded to 10 gigawatts
claims.notes: Background. Independent corroboration of C01 and C02 from a second outlet.

claims.claim: Cole put proven natural gas reserves on Alaska's North Slope at more than 35 trillion cubic feet.
claims.verbatim: more than 35 trillion cubic feet of proven natural gas reserves on Alaska's North Slope
claims.suggested_phrasing: more than 35 trillion cubic feet across the North Slope, by Dermot Cole's count
claims.notes: Background. Deliberately not reconciled with C04.

claims.claim: Borough Mayor Patkotak and three officials from Twenty First Century Utilities presented the project at CERAWeek in March in Texas.
claims.verbatim: Borough Mayor Josh Patkotak and three officials from Twenty First Century Utilities gave a presentation on this massive project at CERA Week in March in Texas
claims.notes: Background. The Alaska Current's May 12th article separately dates a CERAWeek panel to March 23rd, 2026.

claims.claim: The Alaska Current reported in May that the borough will tap its Permanent Fund to help finance the deal, providing a direct equity stake.
claims.verbatim: NSB will tap its $1.3 billion Permanent Fund to help finance the deal, providing a direct equity stake.
claims.suggested_phrasing: the Alaska Current reported in May that the borough's Permanent Fund would help finance the deal
claims.notes: Background, single outlet, no primary reached. Use only with attribution if at all.

claims.claim: Alaska's net summer generating capacity was 2,853 megawatts in 2024.
claims.verbatim: Net summer capacity (megawatts) 2,853
claims.notes: Data year 2024, Alaska Electricity Profile 2024, Table 1. Ranked 48th. Checked 2026-10-04 by the showrunner and the fact-checker. Utilities 2,639 plus IPP and CHP 215 sums to 2,854, a one megawatt rounding difference in EIA's own table.

claims.claim: Electric utilities held 2,639 megawatts of Alaska's 2024 net summer capacity.
claims.verbatim: Electric utilities 2,639
claims.notes: Table 1 capacity sub-row.

claims.claim: Independent power producers and combined heat and power plants held 215 megawatts of Alaska's 2024 net summer capacity.
claims.verbatim: IPP & CHP 215
claims.notes: Table 1 capacity sub-row.

claims.claim: Alaska's net electricity generation was 6,690,506 megawatthours in 2024.
claims.verbatim: Net generation (megawatthours) 6,690,506
claims.notes: Sub-rows 6,020,426 plus 670,080 sum exactly.

claims.claim: Natural gas was Alaska's primary energy source for electricity in 2024.
claims.verbatim: Primary energy source Natural gas
claims.notes: Table 1.

claims.claim: Alaska's average retail electricity price was 22.17 cents per kilowatthour in 2024, ranked 6th among the states.
claims.verbatim: Average retail price (cents/kWh) 22.17
claims.notes: Table 1 rank column shows 6.

claims.claim: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Alaska District posted request for information W911KB279A007, EIE490 Microreactor Synchronization, Eielson AFB, Alaska, on October 2nd.
claims.verbatim: "solicitationNumber": "W911KB279A007", "title": "EIE490 Microreactor Synchronization, Eielson AFB, Alaska", "postedDate": "2026-10-02T23:22:05.640+00:00"
claims.source_outlet: SAM.gov, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Alaska District
claims.notes: Runner-up story. Special notice, market intelligence only.

claims.claim: The Eielson notice describes a 45 megawatt thermal, 5 megawatt electric nuclear microreactor initiative at Eielson AFB.
claims.verbatim: the installation of a 45MWth/5 Mwe nuclear microreactor initiative at Eielson AFB by extending the heating, power, communications and water systems
claims.source_outlet: SAM.gov, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Alaska District
claims.notes: Runner-up story. The requirement is the tie-in, not the reactor itself.

claims.claim: Responses to the Eielson microreactor RFI are due October 16th at 2 PM Alaska time.
claims.verbatim: "responseDate": "2026-10-16T14:00:00-08:00", "responseTimeZone": "America/Anchorage"
claims.source_outlet: SAM.gov, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Alaska District
claims.notes: Runner-up story.

claims.claim: Independent candidate Bill Hill joined other independents in Washington to call for Congress to return and tackle data centers.
claims.verbatim: Independent candidate Bill Hill joined other high-profile Independents in Washington, D.C., on Thursday to call for Congress to return and tackle data centers.
claims.notes: Runner-up. The office Hill seeks was not confirmed verbatim on the page.

claims.claim: Bill Hill said Alaska is in an energy crisis and that data centers would be bought on the backs of ratepayers.
claims.verbatim: We are in an energy crisis in Alaska, and now you want to bring technology to our state that is going to be bought on the backs of ratepayers.
claims.notes: Named-person quote confirmed on the fetched page.

claims.claim: Hill said he did not want data centers to receive tax breaks or to build vast complexes without local input and support.
claims.verbatim: Hill said he didn't want to see data centers receive tax breaks or the ability to build vast complexes without local input and support.
claims.notes: Paraphrase by the outlet; render as reported speech.

claims.claim: Rep. Nick Begich introduced H.R. 8400 on April 21st with Rep. Crenshaw and Rep. Owens.
claims.verbatim: April 21, 2026 Mr. Begich (for himself, Mr. Crenshaw, and Mr. Owens) introduced the following bill
claims.notes: Background, outside window. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

claims.claim: H.R. 8400 may be cited as the DATA Act of 2026.
claims.verbatim: This Act may be cited as the `Decentralized Access to Technology Alternatives Act of 2026' or the `DATA Act of 2026'.
claims.notes: GPO quote marks as printed.

claims.claim: Under H.R. 8400 a consumer-regulated electric utility system must be physically islanded from all regulated utilities, the bulk-power system and the Bulk Electric System.
claims.verbatim: the system is physically islanded from-- (i) all regulated utilities; (ii) the bulk-power system; and (iii) the Bulk Electric System
claims.notes: GPO double hyphen typography as printed.

claims.claim: H.R. 8400 would exempt consumer-regulated electric utilities from Federal Power Act regulation including rate regulation, reliability standards and interconnection requirements.
claims.verbatim: (1) shall be exempt from regulation under the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 791a et seq.), including with respect to-- (A) rate regulation;
claims.notes: Full list (A) to (G) on the page.

claims.claim: EIA's power plant records list 152 power plants in Alaska with 3,106.5 megawatts of installed nameplate capacity.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Power Plants in the U.S. (EIA-860, EIA-860M and EIA-923)
claims.notes: Showrunner query of EIA's public plant feature service, 2026-10-04, data period 202502 (February 2025). Sums of Install_MW (installed nameplate) and Total_MW (maximum summer capacity) over State='Alaska'. Raw response saved at out/2026-10-05/primary/akplants.json. Consistent with EIA's state profile (C25, 2,853 MW net summer for 2024). NSP's 3 and 10 GW are presumably nameplate, so the like-for-like comparison is against 3,106.5.

claims.claim: Those 152 Alaska plants have a combined maximum summer capacity of 2,852.2 megawatts.
claims.verbatim: "summer": 2852.2
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Power Plants in the U.S. (EIA-860, EIA-860M and EIA-923)
claims.notes: Same query as C41.

claims.claim: Alaska's largest power plant by installed capacity is George M Sullivan Generation Plant 2, a natural gas plant of 346.9 megawatts.
claims.verbatim: 'Plant_Name': 'George M Sullivan Generation Plant 2', 'Install_MW': 346.9, 'Total_MW': 309.3, 'Period': '202502', 'PrimSource': 'natural gas'
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Power Plants in the U.S. (EIA-860, EIA-860M and EIA-923)
claims.notes: Ordered by Install_MW descending. Beluga is second at 312.4 MW nameplate. Sullivan Plant 2 is in Anchorage (61.23 N, 149.72 W).

claims.claim: North Slope Borough Power and Light runs seven village power plants, in Atqasuk, Kaktovik, Nuiqsut, Point Hope, Point Lay, Anaktuvuk Pass and Wainwright, with 21.4 megawatts of installed capacity combined.
claims.verbatim: NSB Atqasuk Utility 3.2; NSB Kaktovik Utility 2.6; NSB Nuiqsut Utility 4.4; NSB Point Hope Utility 3.1; NSB Point Lay Utility 2.4; NSB Anaktuvuk Pass 2.7; NSB Wainwright Utility 3 (Install_MW, Utility_Na 'North Slope Borough Power & Light', Period 202502)
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Power Plants in the U.S. (EIA-860, EIA-860M and EIA-923)
claims.notes: Sum 3.2+2.6+4.4+3.1+2.4+2.7+3.0 = 21.4 MW. Six of seven list petroleum as primary source, Nuiqsut natural gas. Utqiagvik's plant (Barrow, 17.3 MW) belongs to a different utility and is not in this sum. Raw response at out/2026-10-05/primary/nsb.json.

claims.claim: The two borough commitments the Alaska Current reports, $1.2 million in November 2025 and $5 million in March, total $6.2 million.
claims.verbatim: In Nov. 2025, Patkotak authorized a $1.2 million no-bid contract for the firm to conduct a feasibility study. ... In March, the North Slope Borough committed another $5 million in public funds to Twenty First Century Utilities
claims.suggested_phrasing: as reported by the Alaska Current
claims.notes: DERIVED by the showrunner, 1.2 + 5.0 = 6.2, from C07 and C08. The word 'another' in C08 makes the two additive. Any other borough spending on the project is not known, so print 'so far' or 'reported'.

claims.claim: North Slope Power's planned 10,000 megawatts would be about 3.2 times the 3,106.5 megawatts of installed capacity in all 152 Alaska power plants, and its 3,000 megawatt first phase about 97 percent of it.
claims.verbatim: with plans to scale to a world record-breaking 10 gigawatts (C02); {"nameplate": 3106.5, "summer": 2852.2, "n": 152} (C41)
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Energy Information Administration, with the Alaska Current
claims.suggested_phrasing: more than three times every power plant in Alaska combined; a first phase about the size of all of them
claims.notes: DERIVED by the showrunner from C02 (10 GW, reported) and C41 (EIA installed nameplate, 3,106.5 MW). 10,000 / 3,106.5 = 3.22; 3,000 / 3,106.5 = 0.966. Nameplate against nameplate is the like-for-like basis; against EIA's 2,853 MW net summer capacity (C25) the ratios are 3.5 and 1.05. Print 'more than three times' and 'about the size of', never 'bigger than' for phase one.
